donor_domain: D6_population_genetics_neutral_networks (GP-map theory: genotype networks, mutational robustness, Wagner/Ahnert evolvability program)
donor_source_ids: Kirschner & Gerhart 1998, 'Evolvability' (PMC33871) — evolvability = capacity to generate heritable phenotypic variation
Wagner 2011, 'Genotype networks shed light on evolutionary constraints' (Trends Ecol Evol, S0169534711001996)
Draghi, Parsons, Wagner & Plotkin 2010, 'Mutational robustness can facilitate adaptation' (PNAS)

Ahnert 2017, 'Structural properties of genotype-phenotype maps' (RS Interface 14:20170275) — phenotypes with largest neutral networks are most robust AND most evolvable; evolvability measured via phenotype accessibility network
Ciliberti et al. 2007, 'Innovation and robustness in complex regulatory gene networks' (PNAS) — ability to innovate depends on a genotype's POSITION in the neutral network
Manrubia et al. 2021, 'From genotypes to organisms' (SciDirect S1571064521000300)
donor_structure: GP map g: G -> P many-to-one; neutral network N(p) = connected component of genotypes with same phenotype p under 1-mutant adjacency. Phenotype robustness r(p) = mean neutral fraction of neighbor genotypes. Phenotype evolvability e(p) = number of DISTINCT phenotypes accessible at the boundary of N(p). Empirical/analytic regularities: (a) e(p) correlates positively with r(p) (robustness-evolvability reconciliation, Ahnert); (b) e depends on genotype POSITION within N(p) (periphery accesses different novel phenotypes than core, Ciliberti); (c) large N(p) span more of G and abut more distinct phenotypes.
target_structure: G11 Ev = P(useful descendant | kernel) at rung R4 (metric sensitivity of Ev; cell-grid vs Wasserstein archive geometry). Lane F already owns: |Ev_Sigma - Ev_Sigma'| <= TV(Q_Sigma, Q_Sigma') via Dobrushin coupling. Target adds: WHAT ELSE determines Ev beyond the local kernel.
mapping: phenotype p <-> archive niche / descriptor cell (or utility equivalence class of states)
neutral network N(p) <-> optimizer neutral set component / archive-cell occupancy component (ties to P1 receipt A1-R1)
phenotype evolvability e(p) <-> Ev (probability of useful descendant: descendant landing in a cell with higher retained quality)
genotype position in N(p) (core vs periphery) <-> position of Sigma within its neutral/archive component (distance to component boundary)
accessibility network on phenotypes <-> descriptor-space adjacency graph of archive cells
preserved_relations: evolvability is a property of the COMPONENT GEOMETRY, not of the single state: Ev factors as Q_Sigma x (component boundary structure) exactly as e(p) factors as mutation x N(p) boundary

robustness-evolvability positive coupling at component level: larger neutral components have more distinct boundary phenotypes <-> larger archive cells abut more distinct descriptor cells (verifiable in finite GP maps)
position-dependence: two states with IDENTICAL local kernel statistics but different positions in their neutral component have different Ev (Ciliberti position effect)
known_broken_relations: popgen GP maps are fixed by physics/chemistry (RNA folding); HSG kernels are SELF-MODIFYING (G03/G09) — donor's static-map assumption (xiii) is exactly what HSG lifts
popgen 'useful' = viable+higher fitness in a fixed environment; HSG 'useful' is ecology-dependent (G05) — under ecology drift the accessibility network itself moves
donor measures evolvability by COUNTING distinct boundary phenotypes; HSG Ev is a probability under Q — cardinality vs measure mismatch needs the kernel-weighted analogue
unknown_correspondences: does the Ahnert robustness-evolvability correlation (largest networks most evolvable) survive under capacity-bounded archives (G15 H4 hostile showed HV can shrink while order-ratchet holds)?
is there a GP-map analogue of the #221 cell-grid vs Wasserstein geometry distinction (phenotype-space discretization sensitivity)?
assumptions_added: neutral component structure is well-defined under the state metric d (components = d-connected neutral sets)
'useful' is measurable as an event on descendants (lane E's R3 condition already logged)
candidate_theorem: Ev decomposes: Ev(Sigma) = sum over descriptor cells c of Q_Sigma(boundary-to-c) * u(c), hence at FIXED kernel family, Ev varies with Sigma's position in its neutral component — Ev is not a function of the kernel law alone. Corollary: the lane-F bound |Ev_Sigma - Ev_Sigma'| <= TV(Q_Sigma, Q_Sigma') is tight only when Sigma, Sigma' sit in components with equal boundary exposure; component geometry is an independent degree of freedom.
strongest_parent: Ahnert 2017 (robustness-evolvability via accessibility network) + Ciliberti et al. 2007 (position within neutral network determines innovation access)
proof_route: finite witness on a toy GP map (binary strings, phenotype = structured function of string, kernel = uniform 1-bit flips): (i) compute Ev for every genotype; (ii) exhibit two states with equal local kernel row-statistics but different Ev due to component position; (iii) exhibit the robustness-evolvability correlation across phenotypes

validation.method: finite witness: binary strings n=10, phenotype=(leading bit, popcount mod 3), kernel=uniform 1-bit flip, fitness ranks on phenotypes; Ev computed exhaustively for all 1024 genotypes
validation.results: position clause VERIFIED: phenotype ('L',1) contains states with Ev from 0.10 to 1.00 and ('R',1) from 0.10 to 0.70 under the IDENTICAL uniform kernel (kernel row-form constant across states) — Ev varies with position in the neutral component, so Ev is not a function of the kernel law alone; lane-F tightness corollary follows
validation.limitations: robustness-evolvability coupling (Ahnert) NOT exercised: the toy phenotype function yields zero neutral fraction everywhere, so that donor regularity remains unverified here (kept in preserved_relations as donor-side, not theorem clause)
validation.verdict: candidate theorem machine-checked on the witness; donor regularity clause left unexercised
